Otsego West Campus High School had 3 multiracial students in 2024-25
G. N. Haley
Three multiracial students were enrolled at Otsego West Campus High School in the 2024-25 school year, an increase of 200% from the previous year, according to the Michigan Department of Education.
Records show Otsego West Campus High School enrolled 19 students in the 2024-25 school year. Multiracial students represented 15.8% of that enrollment, the smallest ethnic group at the school. The largest group was white students, who accounted for 84.2% (16) of the student body.
The school is part of Otsego Public Schools District, whose central office is in Otsego.
Among the district’s six schools, Dix Street Elementary School had the highest multiracial enrollment in the 2024-25 school year.
Academic performance in Michigan remains below pre-pandemic levels. The 2024 NAEP results show the share of students reaching the basic benchmark in core subjects is about 10 percentage points lower than in 2019, except for fourth-grade math, which saw a decline of just 2 points.
Achievement gaps among ethnic groups persist. On average, Hispanic students scored 15 points lower than white students. The gap was wider for Black students, who scored about 30 points lower than their white peers.
